beats.say: Every time an AI generates a photorealistic image or video, it starts with pure random static. How does a neural network sculpt featureless Gaussian noise into coherent reality? The answer evolved from winding diffusion walks to laser-straight flow matching.

Training begins by imagining time running backward. Take clean data and slowly dissolve it into Gaussian noise until no structure remains. Then ask a neural network to learn the velocity vector field that pushes any noisy point smoothly back toward the data.

Flow matching makes that target astonishingly simple. Pair one random noise point x naught with one real data point x one, and draw the straight bridge between them: x t equals one minus t times x naught, plus t times x one. The target velocity is simply the constant vector x one minus x naught.

scenes.title: Curved diffusion versus straight flow matching

beats.say: Classic diffusion models follow curved stochastic differential equations. Because every path bends sharply as noise fades, an ODE solver must take fifty or even a thousand tiny jittery steps just to stay on course.

Rectified flow matching straightens those trajectories out. When the learned velocity field points directly from noise to data, Euler integration barely curves at all. Watch the race: while classic diffusion crawls through fifty zig-zag steps, flow matching crosses the exact same space in just four crisp leaps.
Zoom out from single particles to the entire probability landscape. At time zero, every sample lives inside one smooth Gaussian bell — a single glowing dome of pure uncertainty.

As the continuity equation transports probability mass along the velocity field, that single hill splits, sharpens, and rises into tall multi-modal peaks — each peak a coherent image, voice, or video. Watch individual particle trajectories glide smoothly across the morphing manifold straight to the summits.

scenes.title: Straight paths turn a thousand steps into a blink

beats.say: From modern image generators to real-time video models, flow matching powers today's fastest generative AI. Instead of fighting curved randomness step by painful step, it builds a direct optimal-transport highway from chaos to structure. Straight paths turn a thousand steps into a blink.
